title: Window for a Downward-Shifted Parabola
originalTopic: Viewing window for a translated parabola
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = x^2 - 3 is the parabola y = x^2 moved down 3 units. Find its vertex and zeros, then recommend a window that shows the vertex, both intercepts with the x-axis, and a clear view of the upward arms.

steps.title: Identify the vertex
steps.explanation: With no linear term, the axis of symmetry is x = 0 and the minimum value is -3.
steps.why: The lowest point of an upward-opening parabola sets the required bottom of the y-window.

steps.title: Solve for the zeros
steps.explanation: The curve crosses the x-axis at about -1.732 and 1.732, both comfortably inside a window of width 10 centered at the origin.
steps.why: The intercepts are the features a reader looks for first, so they must not be crowded against the frame.

steps.title: Fix the vertical span from the arms
steps.explanation: Taking x from -5 to 5 makes the arms rise to y = 22, so the window [-5, 5] by [-4, 22] shows the vertex just above the bottom edge and the full opening of the parabola.
steps.why: Choosing the y-max from the endpoint height keeps the parabola's steepness honest instead of artificially flattening it.
